market_holds: Spot $5.005 (sealed baseline, 2026-11-24 18:08 UTC), 2.35% above the 52-week low, -18.6% over 5 sessions and -38.9% over 20. Front-expiry straddle 11.89% over 3 days; event-implied move 5.26% after removing ordinary vol (20d realised 145% annualised); 25-delta skew +13 vol points, so downside is the side being paid for; put/call OI 0.22. Short float 32.1%, short ratio 4.4 (finviz, read 2026-11-24). Consensus FQ4 revenue $126-137M and EPS -$0.26 to -$0.37 depending on vendor, revised down about 21% over 3 months (chartmill/benzinga). Seven prior prints: median |move| 6.06%, 4 of 7 up. The run-in is the sector and bitcoin, not company news. From the Nov 6 close to the Nov 24 intraday print: CLSK -16%, MARA -15%, CIFR -16%, WULF -14%, BTC -20% (75.2k to 59.9k), and QQQ is swinging 5-7% a day (Nov 20 -5.7%, Nov 23 +7.0%). The step down on Nov 4-5 (-26% over two days) is tied to the Texas governor result, which threatens a data-center approval pause, plus the KBW downgrade (to $9.50) and Bernstein's cut ($24 to $11). The line the stock has traded on for a year is the AI/HPC lease story (Sandersville is leased to Meta's subsidiary and funded with the $2.276B notes; Meta also has exclusivity over 885 MW in Texas), with bitcoin as the beta, not mining revenue.
view: CleanSpark has become a leased-to-Meta development story wrapped around a 13.5k BTC treasury and a mining business that is losing money. Almost everything this release can report on the fiscal quarter is already public. Monthly updates give July-September production of 586 + 593 + 529 = 1,708 BTC. At monthly average BTC prices that is roughly $120M of mining revenue, against consensus of $126-137M. A modest revenue miss is likely, and it is the fourth in a row. Bitcoin went from about $58.6k on Jun 30 to about $86.6k on Sep 30, so GAAP will show a large fair-value gain, and headline EPS will very likely beat a negative consensus by a wide margin. Headline EPS is not what moves this stock: in Feb 2026 a large loss came with +22%. The call decides the reaction. Texas will not be resolved inside the window, because ERCOT's Batch Zero verification falls on Dec 10 and the new governor takes office Jan 19, so the likely message is 'still in exclusivity'. That is roughly what a stock down 39% in 20 days already holds. What could move it is balance-sheet action. The closest peer, MARA, opened about +13% on Nov 10 after a revenue miss, on a $1.1B post-quarter BTC sale used to repay debt plus a $500M buyback, while CLSK fell 5% that day. CleanSpark has said it will sell BTC for 'highly accretive opportunities' and did a $460M buyback in Nov 2025, so a similar action is plausible but not evidenced. On the other side: BTC near $60k leaves mining cash margins thin, the BTC-backed lines and the $1.15B converts sit against an equity value of about $1.25B, and the tape is extreme. Next-open noise from BTC and QQQ alone will probably exceed any company signal. With a crowded short (32% of float), a good surprise would move the stock further than a bad one. That argues for a larger move, not a direction. Net: a slight upward lean, far from a bet.
unpriced: Nothing I can show is unpriced with confidence. The only candidate is a capital-return or deleveraging action modelled on MARA's (BTC sale, debt paydown, buyback). The peer's +13% open shows the market rewards that, and CLSK's price shows no sign of expecting it. But I found no dated evidence that CLSK will announce one.

recommendation.reason: The fiscal-quarter numbers are public through the monthly updates (a revenue miss is likely; a GAAP EPS beat from the BTC mark is near certain), and neither has driven the stock. The decisive items, Texas lease progress and balance-sheet or buyback action, are either known to resolve after the window (ERCOT Dec 10) or have no evidence behind them. In a tape where QQQ is moving 6% a day, overnight noise swamps any edge I can see.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A buyback or BTC-funded deleveraging announcement, or a signed Texas or second lease, would make this a clear long. Disclosed BTC-line stress, an equity or ATM raise, or a lapse of Meta's Texas exclusivity would make it a clear short.

self_critique: Down case: bitcoin is at $60k and still sliding, and the tape is in a violent risk-off. The release may disclose BTC sold at low prices to fund opex and capex, drawn BTC-backed lines under pressure, an impairment, or a 'Texas on hold' message. With equity of about $1.25B against $1.15B of converts plus project debt, a bad step reprices the shares outright, and the paid downside skew agrees. Up case: a 32% short float, a stock at its low, and a peer that jumped 13% on capital actions argue my 53 is too timid. Neither side has dated evidence for this release, so I hold near 50.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition was decisive: CLSK's fall is the sector and BTC, which kept me from reading the drawdown as a signal either way. P3's peer and counterparty route (MARA's print) gave the only directional lead. The P7 thresholds correctly kept me at none, because in a tape this violent the window's noise dominates.
